name: Two peaks: deterministic crowding
lesson: In deterministic crowding every child duels the parent it most resembles, so the few individuals on the narrow hill are not pushed out by the crowd on the broad one.
lookFor: Population 40 and seed 23; selection takes every individual once, so nothing here depends on the selection method. The run without crowding (Niching: None, tournaments of 2) has all 40 individuals on the broad hill by generation 20 and never leaves it. With crowding there are 36 individuals near the broad hill and 4 near the narrow one in generation 20, and 35 and 5 in generation 100: both hills stay occupied while the narrow one slowly improves (best 0.95 in generation 100) until a child comes within ε of the top in generation 139, where Run until stop pauses. It is slow and it is not a cure for everything: with seeds 1 to 100 and 200 generations both hills are still occupied in 90 runs against 34 without crowding, but only 48 runs get within ε of the narrow hill's top (17 without it); with a population of 12 both hills are kept in 48 runs, with 60 in 99.
